digest.component_or_area: Dependency advisory handling and CI gating
propositions: A committed lock pins transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against that pin to block all in-flight changes via a gating pip-audit job, regardless of whether the change touched the dependency or caused the vulnerability.

The retry mechanism only handles DB-unreachable failures, making `recheck` ineffective for real findings and creating a time-wasting failure mode where authors attempt recheck as their first instinct.

The distinction between `constraint-dependencies` (which only narrows and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output) and `override-dependencies` (which replaces the requirement) was misunderstood during incident response, leading to confidently recorded wrong conclusions about feasibility.
Gerrit verify lane must block advisories only when a change touches the dependency map (uv.lock, pyproject.toml, lock files), not when it is unrelated to the advisory.
The scheduled main lane must fail visibly and escalate to an owner (via ticket filing with dedup) when a CRITICAL/HIGH advisory is outstanding, to prevent releases on known-vulnerable pins.

A documented runbook must cover: real vs flake findings, why recheck cannot clear real findings, override-dependencies vs constraint-dependencies distinction, evidence required for safe overrides, and verification steps including severity fallback for unrated advisories.
